f3_program: observe(at("natalie.father.savings.amount", "initial"), 10000, "dollar", source("saved up $10,000"))

transfer("natalie_payment", "natalie.father", at("natalie.father.savings.amount", "current"), at("natalie.money.amount", "current"), fraction(at("natalie.father.savings.amount", "initial"), 1, 2), source("Natalie will get half"))

transfer("rick_payment", "natalie.father", at("natalie.father.savings.amount", "current"), at("rick.money.amount", "current"), fraction(at("natalie.father.savings.amount", "current"), 60, 100), source("Rick will get 60 percent of the remaining money"))

transfer("lucy_payment", "natalie.father", at("natalie.father.savings.amount", "current"), at("lucy.money.amount", "current"), at("natalie.father.savings.amount", "current"), source("Lucy will get whatever is left after Natilie and Rick get paid"))
query("value", event_field("lucy_payment", "quantity"))

assumptions: The phrase "twice more than on Monday" can mean either twice Monday's quantity or Monday's quantity plus twice that quantity; the source does not disambiguate these readings.

f3_program: observe(at("company.stock_options.outstanding.weighted_average_exercise_price_per_share", "2019-09-30"), 7.00, "currency_per_share", cell("Outstanding at September 30, 2019", "Weighted-Average Exercise Price Per Share"))
query("value", at("company.stock_options.outstanding.weighted_average_exercise_price_per_share", "2019-09-30"))
assumptions: The question's "price" refers to the table's weighted-average exercise price per share for the outstanding stock options.

f3_program: collection("sixth_grade.students", "student", "survey", source("240 sixth-grade students were asked"))
observe(at("sixth_grade.students.count", "survey"), 240, "count", source("240 sixth-grade students"))
fraction_of(at("sixth_grade.students.monthly_novel_reading.three_or_more.count", "survey"), at("sixth_grade.students.count", "survey"), 1, 6, source("1/6 of students read three or more novels"))
percent_of(at("sixth_grade.students.monthly_novel_reading.two.count", "survey"), at("sixth_grade.students.count", "survey"), 35, source("35% of students read two novels"))
fraction_of(at("sixth_grade.students.monthly_novel_reading.one.count", "survey"), at("sixth_grade.students.count", "survey"), 5, 12, source("5/12 of students read one novel"))

sum_relation(at("sixth_grade.students.count", "survey"), at("sixth_grade.students.monthly_novel_reading.three_or_more.count", "survey"), at("sixth_grade.students.monthly_novel_reading.two.count", "survey"), at("sixth_grade.students.monthly_novel_reading.one.count", "survey"), at("sixth_grade.students.monthly_novel_reading.none.count", "survey"), source("1/6 of students read three or more novels, 35% of students read two novels, 5/12 of students read one novel, and the rest of the students do not read anything"))
query("value", at("sixth_grade.students.monthly_novel_reading.none.count", "survey"))
collection("lisa.pizza.meat_pieces", "meat_piece", "lisa.pizza", source("30 pieces of pepperoni for a pizza, twice as many pieces of ham, and 12 more pieces of sausage than pepperoni"))
observe(at("lisa.pizza.meat_pieces.pepperoni.count", "whole_pizza"), 30, "count", source("30 pieces of pepperoni for a pizza"))
multiple(at("lisa.pizza.meat_pieces.ham.count", "whole_pizza"), at("lisa.pizza.meat_pieces.pepperoni.count", "whole_pizza"), 2, source("twice as many pieces of ham"))
offset(at("lisa.pizza.meat_pieces.sausage.count", "whole_pizza"), at("lisa.pizza.meat_pieces.pepperoni.count", "whole_pizza"), 12, "count", source("12 more pieces of sausage than pepperoni"))
collection("lisa.pizza.slices", "slice", "lisa.pizza", source("6 slices of pizza"))
observe(at("lisa.pizza.slices.count", "whole_pizza"), 6, "count", source("6 slices of pizza"))
collection("lisa.pizza.each_slice.meat_pieces", "meat_piece", "lisa.pizza.each_slice", source("everything was distributed evenly"))

quotient_relation(at("lisa.pizza.each_slice.meat_pieces.pepperoni.count", "current"), at("lisa.pizza.meat_pieces.pepperoni.count", "whole_pizza"), at("lisa.pizza.slices.count", "whole_pizza"), source("there are 6 slices of pizza, and everything was distributed evenly"))

quotient_relation(at("lisa.pizza.each_slice.meat_pieces.ham.count", "current"), at("lisa.pizza.meat_pieces.ham.count", "whole_pizza"), at("lisa.pizza.slices.count", "whole_pizza"), source("there are 6 slices of pizza, and everything was distributed evenly"))

quotient_relation(at("lisa.pizza.each_slice.meat_pieces.sausage.count", "current"), at("lisa.pizza.meat_pieces.sausage.count", "whole_pizza"), at("lisa.pizza.slices.count", "whole_pizza"), source("there are 6 slices of pizza, and everything was distributed evenly"))
query("sum", "lisa.pizza.each_slice.meat_pieces", "current")
assumptions: "Everything" is interpreted as each of the three listed meat types being distributed evenly among the six slices.
